title: Roadstorm versioned benchmark scenario configuration (scenario schema version 1)
description: Machine-readable contract for a benchmark scenario configuration, defined at M0.9 from docs/BENCHMARKS.md ('Reference driver and records', 'AI metrics', 'Tactical comparison') and the ReferenceRun/Scenario row of docs/TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md 'Content contracts' (fixture and driver revisions, initial state/commands/history, seeds, car/loadout/assist/track/handling hashes, measured traces, eligibility and metric version). A scenario fixes the authored configuration of a measurement or a matched comparison: the course and its revision, every dependency revision, the participants of one execution (the fixed context cars plus the single evaluated slot), for a matched comparison the alternative producer arms that run the evaluated slot in separate executions from the same seed, initial state and history (BENCHMARKS compares Classic, cloning-only, Surge and Switch from matched initial states and histories; the compared producers are runs of one slot, never simultaneous cars at one pose), the initial state, the capture/comparison protocol (60 Hz fixed tick, 2 s history warm-up, 3 s opportunity window, 0.10 m / 0.10 m/s handover tolerance), the seeds, the required telemetry and the documented initial targets. The initial state covers the per-participant poses and velocities, the initial commands (an authored schedule or a controller revision) and the shared pre-window history, so two scenarios that declare the same participants cannot silently differ in history (docs/TECHNICAL_DESIGN.md 'Content contracts': initial state/commands/history; docs/BENCHMARKS.md 'Tactical comparison': matched initial states and histories). A scenario is authored configuration, never measured evidence: lap times, medians, contact rates and completed-test outcomes belong to reference records and evaluation reports produced later by M1/M4/M8 tooling, never to a scenario file. A JSON null means 'not yet determined' and MUST be paired with an entry in the enclosing fixture's 'unknowns' (see scenario_fixture.schema.json); an optional member that is absent means 'not applicable'. The safety_interventions telemetry channel is reserved by this contract for tick-level (60 Hz) safety/emergency evidence. Its linked payload lives in the TacticalIntent contract (../intent/tactical_intent.schema.json, schema version 1.1.0 as of this revision): per-tick override exposure is safety.interventions.ticks, and wholesale emergency substitution/reset including persistent Classic replacement is safety.emergency (substituted, kind, tick, persistent, reason). Material-correction magnitude belongs to the 5 Hz corrections record (safety.corrections[*].proposed/applied), not to the tick channel. No intervention payload, count or measurement is authored here; per-intervention magnitude beyond a correction's proposed/applied values and the final intervention category vocabulary remain open until preregistration (recorded in this slice's README). Provenance is recorded once by the enclosing fixture. Companion vocabulary lives in ../common.schema.json; the measured-evidence half of this contract is reference_run.schema.json.

schema_version.description: Contract revision identifier. A scenario whose schema_version differs is rejected, not silently migrated; a contract change requires a new version and a recorded decision.

scenario_id.description: Stable semantic ID, e.g. scenario.tactical.slower_lead_straight. Renaming a scenario requires a new ID and a recorded decision.

scenario_family.description: Which benchmark the scenario instantiates: reference_lap_capture produces the BENCHMARKS reference records; the next six are the 'Tactical comparison' families; 'regression' is reserved for later fixtures added only for meaningful new concerns.

revision.description: Scenario content revision. Any semantic change to dependencies, participants, initial state, protocol, seeds or telemetry bumps this; the enclosing fixture's content_hash is recomputed by the validator.

status.description: provisional = authored initial contract, not yet executed against an implementation; frozen = accepted after review; example = contract illustration that deliberately instantiates unratified producers (e.g. learned_policy participants before M4B) without claiming they exist. 'measured' is not valid here: a scenario carries configuration and targets, never measured outcomes.

course_id.description: Stable semantic course ID; course content is authored at M2.

course_revision.description: Course content revision this scenario runs on. null while course content is unratified (M2); a null requires a matching fixture unknowns entry.

engine_revision.description: Pinned engine revision (TECHNICAL_DESIGN: Godot 4.7.2 Standard, pinned at M0.1). null requires a fixture unknowns entry.

physics_backend.description: M0 pins the built-in Jolt 3D backend; a backend change is a handling revision (TECHNICAL_DESIGN 'Platform and rendering baseline').

handling_revision.description: Motor/car/surface handling revision; a handling change regenerates affected references. null while M1 has not frozen handling; a null requires a fixture unknowns entry.

calibration_driver_revision.description: Revision of the CalibrationDriver controller code; a controller change is a dependency change recorded before reruns. null until M1.7 builds it; a null requires a fixture unknowns entry.

classic_planner_revision.description: Revision of the Classic planner implementation. null until M4.2; a null requires a fixture unknowns entry.

learned_policy_revision.description: Revision of the Roadstormer learned policy. null until M4B; a null requires a fixture unknowns entry.

reference_line_revision.description: Revision of the authored reference line / speed profile the calibration driver follows. null until M1; a null requires a fixture unknowns entry.

metric_version.description: Revision of the metric definitions this scenario is evaluated under (docs/BENCHMARKS.md). A threshold change requires a recorded decision before evaluating a candidate.

dependencies.description: Every dependency revision a captured result would depend on. Reference records are regenerated when these change (BENCHMARKS 'Reference driver and records').

participants.description: Cars taking part in one execution of the scenario, at most the standard eight-car field. The compared producers of a matched comparison are not extra participants: they are the arms of the comparison member, each a separate execution of this same scenario driving one evaluated slot, so no two compared cars are ever on the track together.

entry_speed_m_s.description: Authored initial forward speed of the evaluated participant. Absent when not applicable (e.g. a standing-start capture); null means undetermined and requires a fixture unknowns entry. When per_participant_state is present it must agree with the evaluated participant's entry.

forward_gap_m.description: Authored initial forward gap to the car ahead. Absent when not applicable. When per_participant_state is present it must agree with the evaluated participant's entry.

lateral_offset_m.description: Authored initial lateral offset from the centerline; positive is right. Absent when not applicable. When per_participant_state is present it must agree with the evaluated participant's entry.

note.description: Authoring provenance for values BENCHMARKS does not fix, e.g. 'authored initial value; BENCHMARKS specifies the warm-up and window, not the entry speed'.

per_participant_state.description: Per-participant initial state. BENCHMARKS compares the evaluated drivers 'from matched initial states and histories', so a multi-participant scenario cannot be pinned by the single-participant members alone; the validator requires an entry for the evaluated participant of a tactical family, requires the single-participant members to agree with that entry, and rejects two entries that name the same `ahead_slot` and declare the same relative pose, because such cars are provably co-located; without a shared named reference an identical tuple can be a legal convoy spaced through different predecessors. Entries also cover the fixed context participants of the one execution. Absent when not applicable (e.g. a single-participant capture).

initial_state.description: Authored initial state, commands and history of the scenario (TECHNICAL_DESIGN 'Content contracts'). All values are authored configuration, never measurements.

tick_rate_hz.description: Fixed simulation tick rate (TECHNICAL_DESIGN 'Fixed tick and movement ownership').

handover_max_position_m.description: Matched comparisons allow at most 0.10 m initial-position handover differences (BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison').

handover_max_speed_m_s.description: Matched comparisons allow at most 0.10 m/s initial-speed handover differences.

history_warmup_s.description: Fixed two-second history warm-up before an opportunity window begins (BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison'; see $defs.constants). Required for tactical families; absent for reference_lap_capture.

opportunity_window_s.description: Opportunity window length, up to three seconds or until the encounter ends (see $defs.constants). Required for tactical families; absent for reference_lap_capture.

race_seed.description: Whole-race seed; rates and intervals are reported by whole independent race/scenario seed (BENCHMARKS 'AI metrics').

scenario_seed.description: Scenario seed the opportunity window begins from (BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison').

seeds.description: Authored seeds. Seeds are configuration, not evidence: recording them costs no measurement.

required_telemetry.description: Telemetry channels the capture must record for this scenario to be evaluable. The per-family minimum is fixed in $defs.constants and enforced by the validator. Telemetry distinguishes accepted swept motion, positional correction, reset and route-local projection (BENCHMARKS 'Racing and progress fixtures'); only legal swept motion crosses gates. Two safety channels are distinguished: safety_corrections carries the proposed 5 Hz intent's material road/collision corrections with proposed/applied magnitudes (one intent corrected on several 60 Hz ticks is counted once at the intent level), while safety_interventions carries the tick-level (60 Hz) safety/emergency records behind them - the per-tick override exposure (TacticalIntent safety.interventions.ticks) and wholesale emergency substitution/reset including persistent replacement by Classic (TacticalIntent safety.emergency) - so BENCHMARKS can count emergency replacements per proposed 5 Hz intent and also report tick-level exposure (BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison'; OPPONENT_AI 'Safety interventions': emergency substitution/reset is separate from material corrections).

evaluated_slot.description: Slot of the single evaluated participant the arms drive. Must name a participant of this scenario whose role is 'evaluated' (the validator checks both).

arms.description: The compared producers, each a driver spec. Every arm is a separate execution of this scenario with the same seed, initial state and history: exactly one arm's car is on the track at a time, so matched comparisons never place two compared cars at one pose and each compared producer is traffic only for the fixed context participants. BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison' compares Classic, cloning-only, Surge and Switch from matched initial states and histories; covering those four producers is a benchmark-level requirement across the six families, while each scenario must declare at least two distinct producer arms and may instantiate any subset of them. The validator enforces the per-scenario minimum plus producer identity and style coherence for the six tactical families. Arm results are reported per arm_id.

comparison.description: Matched-comparison structure: which slot is evaluated and which producer arms are compared in it. Required for the six tactical families (the validator enforces this); absent for a reference capture, where one calibration-driver subject runs alone.

record_id.description: ID of the reference record this scenario is matched against; must resolve to a record embedded in the enclosing fixture.

revision.description: Reference revision. BENCHMARKS: match an evaluated Roadstormer and Classic by car, loadout, difficulty, assists, initial scenario and reference revision.

reference.description: Absent when the scenario itself captures the reference (reference_lap_capture) or when no reference record exists yet.

reason.description: Documented reason a window may be excluded before counting results (BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison').

count.description: Windows excluded under this rule by the most recent evaluation; 0 in an authored configuration because no evaluation has run yet.

exclusions.description: Invalid windows are excluded with a documented reason before counting results, and the excluded counts are reported.

slot.description: Stable slot name inside the scenario, e.g. 'lead', 'traffic_1' or 'evaluated'.

role.description: Role in the comparison. 'evaluated' is the single evaluated slot of a matched comparison: BENCHMARKS compares Classic, cloning-only, Surge and Switch from matched initial states and histories, and those producers are alternative runs of this one slot declared in the scenario's comparison.arms - never simultaneous participants - so no two compared cars share a pose. Exactly one participant may carry it (the validator checks). 'reference_subject' is the single calibration-driver subject of a reference capture; 'slower_lead', 'traffic' and 'proxy' are fixed context participants present in every run of the scenario. Every non-evaluated participant declares its own driver; the evaluated slot's producers are its arms, so it carries no driver member of its own (the validator checks both directions).

car_id.description: Car definition ID; the balanced starter is car.balanced_starter (BENCHMARKS).

loadout.description: Loadout under test. The standard medal session uses the balanced starter at levels 0/0/0, i.e. stock.

assists.description: Assist set; BENCHMARKS uses Standard drift/stability assists for reference and comparison drivers.

kind.description: calibration_driver is the BENCHMARKS fixed reference path follower; classic_planner is the Classic racer; cloning_only_policy and learned_policy are the behavioral-cloning-only and PPO-trained Roadstormer producers compared in 'Tactical comparison'; human_proxy is an original scripted noisy test driver, not evidence of real human interaction.

difficulty.description: Explicit difficulty input. Absent when the driver has no difficulty input (calibration driver, proxies, scripted drivers). A compared producer arm must carry the matched difficulty: BENCHMARKS matches evaluated producers by car, loadout, difficulty, assists, initial scenario and reference revision, so arms of one comparison share one difficulty.

style.description: Explicit style input. 'none' is the Classic-only style pair 0/0. Absent when the driver has no style input.

producer_revision.description: Revision of the producer implementation behind this driver, so producers are pinned by an explicit revision rather than by an undocumented convention. Required for cloning_only_policy, which no dependencies member pins: BENCHMARKS/OPPONENT_AI evaluate the behavioral-cloning-only producer separately from the PPO-trained policy, and the two are distinguished only by this revision. learned_policy producers are pinned by dependencies.learned_policy_revision. null while the producer is unratified; a null requires a fixture unknowns entry.

arm_id.description: Stable name of the compared producer within this scenario, e.g. 'classic', 'cloning_only', 'surge' or 'switch'. Unique inside the scenario (the validator checks); results are reported per arm.

comparison_arm.description: One compared producer: a driver spec that runs the evaluated slot in a separate execution of this scenario, from the same seed, initial state and history as every other arm. An arm is a run, not a car: two arms are never on the track together, which is what keeps the matched histories of BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison' intact. Every arm carries the same matched difficulty. For the six preregistered tactical families the compared producers are classic_planner, cloning_only_policy and learned_policy (Surge/Switch are learned-policy styles); human_proxy and scripted drivers are fixed context participants, not compared producers. A scenario may instantiate any subset of at least two distinct producers.

slot.description: Participant slot this entry fixes; must name a participant of this scenario (the validator checks it).

ahead_slot.description: Slot of a different car ahead that forward_gap_m is measured to; a participant may not name itself (the validator rejects direct self-reference). Optional because existing single-car-follow authoring does not need it, but required to make two relative poses comparable: without a shared named reference, identical (gap, lateral offset, speed, heading) tuples can be a legal convoy spaced through different predecessors. The pose-identity check only compares entries that name the same declared participant ahead; mutual references between distinct cars are not restricted because a closed course has no absolute predecessor ordering.

forward_gap_m.description: Authored initial forward gap to the car ahead. Absent when not applicable; null means undetermined and requires a fixture unknowns entry.

lateral_offset_m.description: Authored initial lateral offset from the centerline; positive is right. Absent when not applicable.

speed_m_s.description: Authored initial forward speed. Absent when not applicable.

heading_offset_deg.description: Authored initial heading offset from the road tangent. Absent when not applicable.

participant_initial_state.description: One participant's authored initial state. The evaluated slot carries the matched initial state every arm starts from, so one authored state serves all compared runs; fixed context participants carry their own. Two entries are only flagged as sharing a place when they name the same ahead_slot and both author equal forward_gap_m and lateral_offset_m numbers: that fixes one route-frame position at t0, while differing speed or heading does not move a car. A null or absent gap or lateral position is undetermined and is never treated as equal. Without a shared named reference, equal positions can be a legal convoy and are not compared.

source.description: How the initial commands are fixed. authored_schedule: the schedule member carries the authored command trace (the validator requires it to be non-empty). controller_revision: a controller revision produces the commands; controller_revision names it, and an absent controller_revision means the driving participant's own driver revision. stored_snapshot: a stored snapshot replays them. none: no authored initial commands apply.

controller_revision.description: Revision of the controller that produces the initial commands. Absent means the driving participant's own driver revision (dependencies); null means undetermined and requires a fixture unknowns entry.

schedule.description: Authored initial command schedule; required when source is 'authored_schedule' (the validator enforces it). A schedule is authored configuration, never evidence: it fixes inputs, not outcomes.

initial_commands.description: How the scenario's initial commands are fixed (TECHNICAL_DESIGN 'Content contracts': initial state/commands/history; BENCHMARKS 'Handling fixtures': a command schedule or controller revision).

t_s.description: Time of the command relative to the scenario start, in seconds.

steer.description: Authored steering input in [-1, 1]; positive is right.

command_step.description: One authored command step of an initial command schedule. A full 60 Hz trace over the warm-up and window is expressible; a controller revision may replace it where the controller is the pinned dependency.

source.description: How the shared pre-window history is established. replay_from_seed: the recorded scenario seed is replayed for the fixed warm-up (BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison'). stored_scenario_snapshot: a stored snapshot is replayed when measured repeatability needs it; snapshot_id and snapshot_revision are then required (the validator checks).

snapshot_id.description: ID of the stored scenario snapshot; required when source is 'stored_scenario_snapshot'. null means undetermined and requires a fixture unknowns entry.

snapshot_revision.description: Revision of the stored scenario snapshot; required when source is 'stored_scenario_snapshot'. null means undetermined and requires a fixture unknowns entry.

warmup_s.description: Length of the shared history before the window opens; absent means protocol.history_warmup_s, and a present value must equal it (the validator checks). null means undetermined and requires a fixture unknowns entry.

scenario_history.description: How the matched pre-window history of a tactical comparison is established, so two scenarios that declare the same participants cannot differ in history (BENCHMARKS 'Tactical comparison': matched initial states and histories; stored scenario snapshots if measured repeatability needs them).

constants.description: Single source of truth for the numeric protocol of this contract, all from docs/BENCHMARKS.md. The fixtures/scenario validator reads these instead of restating them.

history_warmup_s.description: An opportunity window begins from a recorded scenario seed after a fixed two-second history warm-up.

opportunity_window_s.description: The window lasts up to three seconds or until the encounter ends.

reference_lap_capture.description: Minimum telemetry for a reference capture: what BENCHMARKS says must be retained per car/course revision (times, sector splits, speed samples, hashes, validity) plus the events whose presence invalidates a run (contacts, resets, missed gates, progress corrections).

tactical_families.description: Minimum telemetry for a tactical comparison window: the proposed intents, the 5 Hz safety corrections, the tick-level (60 Hz) safety/emergency intervention events BENCHMARKS counts per proposed 5 Hz intent with tick-level exposure also reported, and the commands, poses, contacts, gates and race RNG state the labels and rates are computed from.
